claim: The house holds that its names (Clos Sainte-Hune, Frédéric Émile) guarantee more than the cru system's politics — so the labels omit 'grand cru'
because: Trimbach now bottles and labels four grand crus: Riesling Grand Cru Geisberg (first vintage 2009, released 2015), Grand Cru Schlossberg (2014, released 2017), Grand Cru Mandelberg (2016) and Grand Cru Brand (2018), according to Trimbach's own wine list. The house still keeps Clos Sainte-Hune (in Rosacker) and Frédéric Émile (Geisberg and Osterberg) off the grand cru label, so the stance survives only for those two brands. The accept item 'brands trump crus' is also no longer a fair summary of the house's position.
fix: The house long held that its own names (Clos Sainte-Hune in Rosacker, Frédéric Émile from Geisberg and Osterberg) guarantee more than the cru system, so those flagships still omit 'grand cru'. Since the 2009 Geisberg (released 2015) it has also bottled Grand Cru Geisberg, Schlossberg, Mandelberg and Brand under the cru name.
